dependencies.description: Both separately smoothed laboratory determinations were converted to ITS-90 in the same published reanalysis. The NBS column combines NBS datasets; the BM column combines selected BM datasets. These are not raw measurements, and this author imports no fitting coefficients.
Both columns use the same molar-mass convention specified on printed p56 of the reanalysis; no modern atomic-weight replacement is performed.

Published saturation corrections and temperature conversion depend on common auxiliary density and vapor-pressure descriptions. Underlying auxiliary originals were not independently audited; their covariance and propagated uncertainty remain unquantified.
Distinct laboratory calorimeters ultimately use NBS-calibrated electrical and thermometric standards; this is shared calibration lineage, not independent uncertainty.
Some experiments in the two laboratory composites used Calorimetry Conference n-heptane supplied by NBS; other experiments used different samples. Partial common sample provenance is retained.

The WebBook guide calls C_p,gas ideal-gas heat capacity. A p=1 bar standard-state table comment is not a measured finite-pressure Cp value. Original temperature scale and detailed calculation lineage remain unresolved here.

series.reference: Pure neutral liquid n-heptane reference substance on its liquid-vapor coexistence curve; C_sat = T (dS/dT)_sat, not C_p and not dH_sat/dT. Molar basis is the legacy molar-mass convention of Zabransky/Ruzicka p56. No additive enthalpy/entropy zero is needed for this derivative. Exact tabulated ITS-90 temperatures only; no pressure number, mixture, interpolation or extrapolation inferred.

primary.locator: Printed p58, Table 2, NBS column, row given by each literal temperature; original 298.16 K point reprocessed to ITS-90 298.15 K
primary.processing: Published, separately smoothed NBS composite after source temperature/heat-capacity conversion. Primary is designated prospectively as the first laboratory column, without averaging or optimizing against the second column.

uncertainty.unquantified_reason: No separate total uncertainty or covariance for each transformed Table 2 point is supplied. Historical experimental accuracy does not quantify all temperature, auxiliary-property, smoothing and molar-mass dependencies.

historical_accuracy.locator: Printed p144 section 2.5 and footnote 4; original low-temperature calorimetry, 50-370 K
historical_accuracy.interpretation: Authors call this probable error and explicitly say it cannot be computed statistically: their estimate is seldom exceeded. It is not a standard deviation, confidence interval, or total transformed-table uncertainty.

comparison.locator: Printed p58, Table 2, BM column, same ITS-90 temperature row as NBS
comparison.processing: Published, separately smoothed Bureau of Mines composite of selected measurements made with distinct calorimeter vessels and thermometers. Independent experimental origin from NBS, with shared processing and partial sample/calibration lineage explicitly retained.

uncertainty.unquantified_reason: Total uncertainty of each transformed BM table point and correlations with NBS are not quantified. Historical claimed accuracy is retained without probabilistic interpretation or reduction by combining laboratories.

historical_accuracy.locator: Printed p9, discussion of precision and accuracy above 30 K
historical_accuracy.interpretation: Conservative claimed accuracy of original experimental heat capacities; not a standard deviation or a quantified uncertainty of the later ITS-90 reanalysis.

admission.rationale: Original NBS and Bureau of Mines methods, apparatus and tables were checked. Table 2 supplies separate determinations at the same ITS-90 state and quantity. Shared conversion, auxiliaries, standards and partial sample provenance are explicit; admission means provenance-reviewed distinct experiments, not independent error distributions or full model qualification.
